name: Nautobot
what_it_is: Nautobot is a web-based network infrastructure management platform (Network Source of Truth) built on Django, providing a centralized database and automation hub for network operations with REST API, GraphQL, and a plugin system. It is a fork and evolution of NetBox with added automation capabilities, native Git integration, and Celery-based background task processing.
components: postgresql (relational database, referenced as db dependency)
plugin system (custom models, APIs, UI extensions)
configuration: custom fields on any data model
data validation rules (naming standards, custom validators)
Git repositories for config context loading
authentication and permissions (LDAP, SSO via plugins)
modes: development mode (watchmedo auto-restart, local Docker image)
optional selenium profile (browser automation / UI testing)
optional mkdocs profile (documentation server on port 8001)
constraints: Requires PostgreSQL as the relational database backend (MySQL supported but PostgreSQL is primary)
Requires Redis for Celery task queue and caching — cannot run without it
Plugin installation requires application restart and potential database migrations
Git integration only loads YAML data files as config contexts — not arbitrary file types
No built-in network device communication or configuration push — automation relies on external tools or plugins
Multi-tenancy is not native; requires plugin-based extensions for full tenant isolation
notable_absences: No built-in SNMP polling or telemetry collection
No alerting or notification engine (relies on webhooks to external systems)
